name: Bullet

team.summary: Founders Adi and Alex are YC S26 founders fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel, where they built background in optimization and agent context.

evidence.quote: Hi HN! We’re Adi and Alex, founders of Bullet, a faster coding agent.
We were fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel, and naturally thought we were on a sure path to startup success.

product.summary: Bullet is a faster coding agent harness featuring model routing, targeted search, aggressive context hygiene, and parallel execution.

evidence.quote: Bullet is a faster coding agent
Same model → tools → results pattern. A tighter loop around it.

size_hint.summary: Target market consists of developers and software engineers utilizing coding agents who experience latency issues.

evidence.quote: We hope that you guys try out Bullet if you are suffering with speed as much as we were

competitors.summary: Commenters and post text mention several competing coding agents, harnesses, and tools like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and mini-SWE-agent.

evidence.quote: Let’s take on Claude Code and Codex, we can do it!
evidence.author: hn_post

why_now.summary: Coding agents like Claude Code and Codex have gained massive usage, but engineers suffer from slow iteration speed and high latency.

evidence.quote: We were spending hours waiting for coding agents like Claude Code and Codex

risks.risk: Proprietary software model lacking open-source code makes users hesitant to trust it with root access and binary execution.

evidence.quote: So, I am supposed to just give a random binary on a website that may or may not be malware... and I am not even allowed to review the code?

risks.risk: Many commenters note that harness improvements can easily be replicated via prompting or custom scripts, raising defensibility questions.

evidence.quote: Proprietary software is no longer a moat, and for something like this it just makes your software very hard to trust.

risks.risk: History of numerous rapid pivots prior to landing on this product idea.

evidence.quote: So, Bullet started as an AI hedge fund, a browser-use agent, synthetic financial data (oof), a mobile IDE, and a bunch of other things.

founder_depth.why: Founders have technical backgrounds at quantitative and ad-tech firms (AppLovin, Citadel) and have shipped multiple product iterations, but lack deep long-term open-source domain history in this specific category.

evidence.quote: We were fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel

shipping_evidence.why: The product is live with a downloadable client, CLI installation via npm, and benchmark test results published.

evidence.quote: On SWE-bench Verified, Bullet resolved 479/500 (95.8%) in one attempt

demand_signal.why: Solid HN launch engagement with 121 points and 89 comments, including users testing it out, though no revenue or named enterprise customers are mentioned.

evidence.quote: I'm giving it a try on a new project I'm spinning up. It does seem faster

defensibility.why: Multiple commenters point out that the harness features can be replicated via prompts, custom scripts, or open-source configurations.

evidence.quote: Proprietary software is no longer a moat, and for something like this it just makes your software very hard to trust.

analysis.thesis_fit_reason: Bullet is an AI dev tool coding agent harness used by software engineers, offered as free software downloads and CLI packages.
analysis.case_summary: Strong shipping velocity and active engagement on launch day, offset by concerns over software defensibility and closed-source trust.
would_change_my_mind: Open-sourcing the harness repository to address supply chain security concerns.
Demonstrating strong recurring revenue or retention metrics from engineering teams.
Proving structural technical advantages that cannot be replicated via standard prompting.
data_gaps: GitHub repository link or open-source availability
Details on active user retention and usage frequency
